newsitem.title: PERU: Suspected MRTA rebels attack Lima store, start fire.
newsitem.headline: Suspected MRTA rebels attack Lima store, start fire.

text.p: Suspected Marxist rebels burst into a textile store in Lima on Saturday, throwing grenades that sparked a large fire in which at least two firefighters were injured, police said.
"It's a terrorist attack. They used hand grenades," police bomb squad officer Carlos Samaniego told Reuters.
Peruvian anti-terrorist police confirmed the attack in Lima's working class La Victoria district was carried out by rebels of the Tupac Amaru Revolutionary Movement (MRTA).
About 20 MRTA members are holding 72 hostages at the Japanese ambassador's home in Lima in a siege which has so far lasted 88 days.

Police, quoting witnesses, said heavily armed rebels entered the store, which also operates a wool-products factory, and shouted MRTA slogans before the fire broke out shortly after 3:00 P.M. local time (2000 GMT).
They also said they found MRTA slogans painted on the walls outside the building.
"They threw the grenades as they shouted their slogans," said Samaniego, adding details were scarce because bomb squad officials had yet to enter the building.
The MRTA seized hundreds of VIP hostages when it stormed the diplomatic compound on Dec. 17 and continues to hold its most prized bargaining chips.
Among the captives still held are President Alberto Fujimori's brother Pedro, the envoys of Japan and Bolivia and two dozen Japanese diplomats and businessmen.
